candidates.explanation: I couldn't see the source, so this is inferred from the graph. Login and refresh work, and refresh uses the separate JwtRefreshStrategy. Only access-token verification fails, so the passport-jwt strategy is probably verifying with the wrong key. The likely cause is that secretOrKey reads the wrong config entry, such as the refresh secret, instead of auth.secret. A wrong extractor or ignoreExpiration setting is also possible. A signature mismatch would make passport reject every access token with 401.

validate() decides whether the decoded payload is accepted. It may check a claim the token doesn't carry, for example a different field name than the id that getTokensData signs. It may also be inverted and throw UnauthorizedException for valid payloads. Either would give a 401 for every fresh token even when the signature is valid.

This method signs the access token. If it signs with a different secret, such as the refresh secret, or puts the wrong claims in the payload, the token won't verify in JwtStrategy. Login and refresh would still appear to work, because they only issue tokens, while protected endpoints return 401.

fix.description: Make the access-token secret consistent between signing and verification. JwtStrategy's secretOrKey should read auth.secret via configService.getOrThrow('auth.secret', { infer: true }), the same key getTokensData uses to sign the access token. Also make sure validate() only rejects a payload that really lacks id, and returns the payload otherwise.

candidates.explanation: I couldn't see the source, so this is inferred from the graph. Login and refresh work, and refresh uses the separate JwtRefreshStrategy. Only access-token verification fails, so the passport-jwt strategy is probably verifying with the wrong key. The likely cause is that secretOrKey reads the wrong config entry, such as the refresh secret, instead of auth.secret. A wrong extractor or ignoreExpiration setting is also possible. A signature mismatch would make passport reject every access token with 401.

validate() decides whether the decoded payload is accepted. It may check a claim the token doesn't carry, for example a different field name than the id that getTokensData signs. It may also be inverted and throw UnauthorizedException for valid payloads. Either would give a 401 for every fresh token even when the signature is valid.

This method signs the access token. If it signs with a different secret, such as the refresh secret, or puts the wrong claims in the payload, the token won't verify in JwtStrategy. Login and refresh would still appear to work, because they only issue tokens, while protected endpoints return 401.

fix.description: Make the access-token secret consistent between signing and verification. JwtStrategy's secretOrKey should read auth.secret via configService.getOrThrow('auth.secret', { infer: true }), the same key getTokensData uses to sign the access token. Also make sure validate() only rejects a payload that really lacks id, and returns the payload otherwise.
